prompt.context: Our client, Berry Chill Frozen Yogurt, is the industry's best quality frozen yogurt made from real California milk and served with a wide array of flavors and toppings. Founded in 2006, the young yogurt chain is popular partly due to its self-serve format and because it is relatively inexpensive compared to other yogurt businesses such as Pinkberry. Over the past two years, the company has opened an average of 10 stores per year (currently has 25 stores) and increased revenue by an annual CAGR of 35%. The case takes place in 2008.
prompt.question: The CEO of Berry Chill has come to us to identify how to increase its current growth path. How would you approach this?

clarifying_info.a: All 25 stores are currently owned and operated in Southern California.

clarifying_info.q: How does the pricing model work?
clarifying_info.a: The company currently sells yogurt only on a per-ounce basis.

clarifying_info.q: Does the company develop its own flavors?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, Berry Chill develops its own proprietary flavors; toppings are generic.
Berry Chill was one of the first in the self-serve frozen yogurt market. In the last year, a few competitors have begun to enter the Southern California market.

clarifying_info.q: What are the major cost drivers?
clarifying_info.a: Major costs are fixed; variable cost is essentially yogurt and toppings.

clarifying_info.q: How is frozen yogurt perceived in the market?
clarifying_info.a: Frozen yogurt is seen as a healthier alternative to ice cream and other desserts. Self-serve style stores are gaining popularity relative to traditional full-service stores.

framework: Current store revenue growth: identify ways to grow revenue from existing 25 stores (pricing, product mix, customer frequency, store hours)
New store expansion: evaluate organic expansion within Southern California and into new geographies (warm weather markets)
New revenue streams / business model: consider franchising, new product lines (coffee, baked goods), catering, or retail/CPG channels
Prioritization criteria: magnitude of revenue impact, ease/speed of execution, investment required, risk to brand, short-run vs. long-run timing

questions.prompt: Walk me through your framework for how Berry Chill can increase its growth path.
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure the problem around existing stores vs. new stores and short-run vs. long-run levers. A strong answer identifies both demand-side (traffic, ticket size) and supply-side (new locations, new channels) opportunities without fixating on cost reduction. Better candidates proactively raise franchising and think about how each idea is actually brought to market.

questions.prompt: How would you evaluate the potential growth strategies you proposed in your framework? Which criterion is most important for Berry Chill to consider?
questions.guidance: Candidate should propose a structured evaluation matrix. Key criteria include: (1) Magnitude of revenue impact — the most important, as the client's goal is to accelerate growth; (2) Difficulty/speed of execution; (3) Capital required; (4) Risk to brand/quality; (5) Timing (short-run vs. long-run). Better candidates also raise franchise monitoring risk and cannibalization between nearby stores.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the specific growth strategies Berry Chill could pursue, both in the short term and long term?

categories.name: Existing stores — revenue per customer
ideas: Introduce premium topping bundles or combo pricing
Add complementary food items: cookies, coffee, smoothies, baked goods
Introduce loyalty/rewards program to drive repeat visits

categories.name: Existing stores — customer volume
ideas: Partnerships with local gyms, schools, or offices
Catering for events and corporate accounts
Seasonal promotions to drive off-peak traffic

categories.name: New store expansion
ideas: Accelerate company-owned store openings within Southern California
Expand into other warm-weather geographies (Arizona, Texas, Florida)
Enter college campuses or high-traffic malls

categories.name: Franchising
ideas: Adopt a franchise model to scale rapidly with lower capital at risk
Leverage franchisee local knowledge in new markets
License proprietary flavors to franchisees while maintaining brand standards

categories.name: New channels / products
ideas: Sell packaged frozen yogurt through grocery retail
Develop a CPG line of yogurt mixes or toppings

recommendation: Short-term: increase the price per ounce and begin offering additional food items (cookies, coffee, etc.) alongside yogurt to grow revenue per customer visit at existing stores.

Medium- to long-term: adopt a franchising model to expand within Southern California and into other warm-weather geographies, enabling fast and highly scalable growth with low capital risk to the overall company.
risks: Potential cannibalization of sales at current stores if new locations open too close
Too rapid expansion outpacing consumer demand in new markets
Loose franchise monitoring may harm brand quality and reputation
next_steps: Determine the specific steps to design and initiate the franchise model (franchise agreement, training, brand standards)
Pilot the price increase and new food items in a subset of stores to validate impact before rolling out chain-wide
